title: AP Publishes a Tracker of Trump’s Presidential Promises
description_short: AP Publishes a Tracker of Trump’s Presidential Promises
description_medium: The Associated Press page linked to this record is titled “Tracking Trump’s presidential promises” and presents a project about promises made by Trump. This narrower description identifies the cited source as an AP tracking project. The packet supplies no specific pledge, dated status entry, assessment criteria, or example of Trump changing his account. It therefore supports describing the tracker’s subject, but not the earlier claims about high-voltage messaging, ambiguous criteria, or accountability costs. Remove those interpretations unless a specific tracker entry and supporting evidence are supplied.
description_long: The Associated Press page cited for this record is headed “Tracking Trump’s presidential promises.” It is a journalism project about promises attributed to Donald Trump, rather than a report documenting the rhetoric or consequences asserted in the earlier description. The source supports a narrow entry about AP publishing a tracker on that subject. The packet does not identify which promise the original writer meant, quote the promise, give a dated progress assessment, or explain the standard used to judge delivery. It also supplies no evidence that Trump’s language shifted, that evaluation criteria were unclear, or that this created particular accountability costs. Those propositions cannot be inferred from the existence of a tracker. This draft therefore confines the claim to the cited project and makes no conclusion about any promise’s status or Trump’s messaging. A specific dated tracker card would be needed to write about an individual commitment or AP’s assessment of it.

title: Exclude: Hobby Lobby ruling has no documented Trump connection
description_short: Exclude: Hobby Lobby ruling has no documented Trump connection
description_medium: The supplied material concerns the Supreme Court’s 2014 Burwell v. Hobby Lobby decision, a dispute over whether closely held companies could invoke the Religious Freedom Restoration Act against the contraceptive-coverage requirement. It does not identify a Trump statement, action, appointment, or role in the case. The cited TrumpFile page’s broad claim about corporations having human rights also exceeds the case-specific holding described in the packet. No source-bounded Trump event can be drafted from this evidence. Exclude this record from Trump-focused coverage unless a documented connection is provided.
description_long: The material supplied for this record describes Burwell v. Hobby Lobby, decided by the Supreme Court in 2014. The case addressed a narrow statutory question: whether closely held for-profit companies could seek a Religious Freedom Restoration Act exemption from the Affordable Care Act’s contraceptive-coverage requirement. That holding is not a general declaration that corporations possess all the rights of natural persons. More fundamentally for this collection, the packet identifies no Trump statement, policy, appointment, or other action connected to the case or decision. A description of the Supreme Court ruling alone would turn a general legal event into a Trump entry without evidence linking Trump to it. The cited TrumpFile URL supplies the page being corrected but no documented nexus in the provided materials. The proposed disposition is exclusion from Trump-focused records unless an attributable Trump action or statement about this decision is sourced. The exact gap is a primary statement, contemporaneous report, or record showing that connection; the case summary cannot substitute for it.
notes: Reason: The supplied title says the Court gave corporations human rights generally, but the described Hobby Lobby holding was limited to a specific RFRA claim by closely held companies.
Proposed correction: Retitle to state that the Court allowed the closely held companies in Hobby Lobby to claim a RFRA exemption from the contraceptive-coverage rule.

Needs context: The focused TrumpFile page describes the 2014 Hobby Lobby decision and makes a broad claim about corporate rights, but contains no Trump statement or action connected to the case. A documented Trump-specific link is missing; the supplied case account also describes a narrower RFRA holding than the page's general human-rights framing.

title: Ivanka Trump Testifies in DC Inquiry into Inaugural Committee Spending
description_short: Ivanka Trump Testifies in DC Inquiry into Inaugural Committee Spending
description_medium: On December 1, 2020, Ivanka Trump sat for a deposition with the D.C. attorney general’s office during its investigation into the 2017 Trump Presidential Inaugural Committee. ABC News reported that the inquiry examined committee spending at the Trump International Hotel. Her lawyer said she connected the parties and told the hotel to charge a fair-market rate. The report describes investigative allegations and testimony; it identifies no knowingly false answer or finding of perjury. The original title’s claim that she lied under oath is unsupported and is omitted.
description_long: On December 1, 2020, Ivanka Trump gave a deposition to the Washington, D.C., attorney general’s office during its investigation of the Trump 2017 Presidential Inaugural Committee. ABC News reported that investigators were examining committee spending, including payments for event space at the Trump International Hotel in Washington. The D.C. attorney general’s filing compared a $5,000 charge for a prayer breakfast using the venue earlier on Inauguration Day with the committee’s later $175,000 payment for the same event space. Ivanka Trump’s lawyer told ABC that her role was limited to connecting the parties and instructing the hotel to charge a fair-market rate. These are reported investigative allegations and an attorney’s characterization of her role, not a judicial finding about her conduct. The available report confirms the deposition but does not quote an answer proved knowingly false, describe a perjury charge, or report a perjury finding. The supported event is her testimony in the civil inquiry. The accusation in the former title is not established by the sources and must not be presented as fact.
notes: The AP report confirms Ivanka Trump’s deposition and describes the lawsuit’s allegations about inaugural-committee payments, but identifies no knowingly false answer or perjury finding. The title’s central accusation remains unsupported.

The linked AP URL returned HTTP 403 during this focused read. proposed_correction: Retitle the entry to describe Ivanka Trump’s deposition in the inaugural-funds lawsuit unless a transcript or official finding substantiates a specific false statement.

title: Exclude: Iran Memorandum and Israeli Restart Warning Are Unsourced
description_short: Exclude: Iran Memorandum and Israeli Restart Warning Are Unsourced
description_medium: The record alleges that Trump signed an “Islamabad Memorandum” with Iran and that Israeli officials warned a conflict could restart within days. Its only cited AP URL concerns Netanyahu’s dispute with Trump over Gaza and Hamas disarmament. That source does not establish the alleged Iran agreement or warning, and the packet names no Israeli official, date, quotation, or conflict-specific statement. No narrower Iran event claim can be responsibly drafted from this evidence. Exclude the record or leave it unresolved until an event-specific source is supplied.
description_long: The populated claim describes an “Islamabad Memorandum” signed by Trump with Iran, followed by an Israeli warning that fighting could restart within days. The packet provides no copy or official description of that memorandum. It also identifies no Israeli official who made the alleged warning, no date or quotation, and no source establishing which conflict the warning concerned. The sole linked Associated Press article is identified in the packet as coverage of Netanyahu’s dispute with Trump over Gaza and Hamas disarmament. That is a different subject and cannot be used as evidence for an Iran ceasefire or memorandum. Because the packet contains no source for the central event itself, even a narrower factual account of the alleged Iran development cannot be completed. The precise evidence needed is an authenticated agreement or official record establishing the memorandum, plus dated event-specific reporting or a primary statement identifying the Israeli speaker and the warning. Until those materials are provided, exclude the claim or retain it as unresolved; do not imply that the alleged events occurred.
notes: The populated description says Trump signed an Islamabad Memorandum with Iran and Israeli officials warned that fighting could resume within days. The only linked source is an AP article titled “Netanyahu’s defiance of Trump on Gaza carries risks,” whose URL concerns Gaza and Hamas disarmament, not the Iran memorandum. The packet does not identify the Israeli officials, their statements or the specific conflict they threatened to restart.
proposed_correction: Keep the existing text unchanged; attach a source for the Iran memorandum and the reported Israeli warning, or correct the entry to the separate Gaza event covered by AP.

title: Fact Check Reports Jermaine Thomas’s 2025 Deportation After Citizenship Challenge
description_short: Fact Check Reports Jermaine Thomas’s 2025 Deportation After Citizenship Challenge
description_medium: A July 2025 Yahoo fact check, citing ICE and DHS, reports Jermaine Thomas was deported to Jamaica on May 28, 2025, after courts rejected his U.S. citizenship claim. It says an immigration judge issued a final removal order in 2013 and Thomas was born in Germany to a U.S.-citizen father serving in the Army. The source does not establish that the Supreme Court personally ruled on his case or that he was legally stateless; those claims are omitted.
description_long: A July 2025 fact check carried by Yahoo and identified in the packet as relying on ICE and DHS reports that Jermaine Thomas was deported to Jamaica on May 28, 2025. The account says courts rejected his claim to U.S. citizenship and that an immigration judge had issued a final removal order in 2013. It identifies Thomas as born in Germany to a U.S.-citizen father who was serving in the Army. These are the facts the linked fact check supports and they should remain attributed to that report. The packet’s former long description adds a specific Supreme Court ruling, a conclusion that Thomas had no citizenship anywhere, and personal details sourced to other outlets; the supplied URL and evidence note do not establish those details. This draft does not infer citizenship from the overseas military-base birth or describe the deportation as a consequence of one administration alone. The narrow event is the reported 2025 deportation after a legal challenge to his citizenship status. A court docket or immigration record would be needed to independently detail the proceedings beyond the fact check’s account.

preserved_fields.title: Jermaine Thomas, Born on US Army Base in Germany, Deported to Jamaica He'd Never Visited
preserved_fields.description_short: Jermaine Thomas, Born on US Army Base in Germany, Deported to Jamaica He'd Never Visited
preserved_fields.description_long: In late May 2025, Jermaine Thomas, 39, was shackled at the wrists and ankles and placed on a flight to Kingston, Jamaica — a country he had never been to in his life. Thomas was born in 1986 at a US military hospital in Germany, where his father — a US citizen — was deployed as an Army soldier. His case had reached the US Supreme Court ten years earlier in a dispute over whether children born to US citizen servicemembers on overseas deployments should automatically receive citizenship. The court ruled against him. Thomas had no citizenship anywhere: not the United States (despite his father's decades of military service), not Germany (where he was born), not Jamaica (his father's ancestral homeland), and not Kenya (his mother's birthplace). When reached by CNN, Thomas described himself as legally stateless, calling from a homeless shelter in Kingston. He had no passport, no support network, and no connection to the country. DHS issued a statement calling him a violent, criminal illegal alien from Jamaica and describing Jamaica as his home country — a characterization the Austin Chronicle challenged in direct correspondence with the department, asking in what sense Jamaica was his home country. DHS did not respond. Thomas's case illustrates how the Trump administration's deportation framework was being applied even to people abandoned by the citizenship system because of technical legal gaps — leaving a man stateless on the basis of his father's military service.

notes: needs_context: The supplied Yahoo/Snopes fact-check says a federal appeals court rejected Thomas’s citizenship claim and cites a 2013 final removal order. This conflicts with the preserved long description’s account of an individual Supreme Court ruling and statelessness; that populated field cannot be reconciled from the supplied packet.

evidence_resolution.proposed_action: Replace the unsupported dramatic narrative with an attributed account of the reported deportation and removal/citizenship history; exclude unverified Supreme Court and statelessness assertions.
evidence_resolution.proposed_title_or_claim: Fact Check Reports Jermaine Thomas’s 2025 Deportation After Citizenship Challenge
supported_facts: The supplied fact-check says Thomas was deported to Jamaica on May 28, 2025.
It reports a 2013 final removal order and that courts rejected his U.S. citizenship claim.
It describes Thomas as born in Germany to a U.S.-citizen father serving in the Army.
limitations: The packet provides no underlying court or immigration file.
The supplied source does not substantiate an individual Supreme Court ruling or the claim that Thomas was stateless.

title: Trump Shares an Image of Mike Lee Criticizing Liz Cheney’s January 6 Footage
description_short: Trump Shares an Image of Mike Lee Criticizing Liz Cheney’s January 6 Footage
description_medium: A searchable archive records a Trump Truth Social image post dated November 20, 2023. Its image description says it shows a Mike Lee post to Liz Cheney about January 6 footage, criticizing its selective presentation and questioning federal agents’ presence in the crowd; it also describes a Cheney post with riot footage. This supports a narrow claim that Trump shared an image of Lee’s critique. The archive does not show Trump himself called Cheney a traitor or said she should be jailed; those claims are omitted.
description_long: The linked NBC News article concerns Kash Patel’s comments about pursuing media figures and his later FBI-director nomination; it does not support the claim about Liz Cheney. A Trump Truth Social archive entry provides a narrower source. It identifies an image post from Donald Trump dated November 20, 2023, and describes the attached image as a Mike Lee post directed at Cheney discussing January 6 footage. The archive’s image description says Lee criticized the selective presentation of events and questioned the presence of federal agents among the crowd; it also notes that the image included a Cheney post with a video clip of the Capitol riot. This evidence supports describing the content Trump shared, with attribution to the archive’s image description. It does not establish that Trump authored Lee’s words, called Cheney a traitor, or stated that she should be jailed. Those stronger accusations should not appear without the original post’s readable text or contemporaneous reporting that verifies the exact language and context. The record is therefore narrowed to the documented image post and its described subject.
